newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mid-Atlantic power higher on Eastern heat.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mid-Atlantic power higher on Eastern heat.

text.p: U.S. Mid-Atlantic spot electricity prices rose Tuesday on with warmer-than-expected temperatures and lack of cooling from Hurricane Edouard, industry sources said.

"We're seeing a little bit of heat hype and there was no storm, no Edouard," said one physicals trader, referring to the hurricane which passed by much of the East Coast to head north over the holiday weekend.
Temperatures through much of the Mid-Atlantic were expected to be normal to above-normal through to September 9.

Next day, peak electricity prices in the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Interconnect power pool were said to have traded as high as $25.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) Tuesday morning, but settled down closer to $24.50 in the afternoon, brokers and traders said.
Peak electricity prices for the three-day U.S. Labor Day weekend had been quoted at $17.00-$17.50 per MWh late last week.
Off-peak PJM power prices for Wednesday delivery were said to be near $15.00 from a weekend range of $15.50-$16.50.
PJM electricity for the four remaining days of this week was quoted at $23.75-24.50 from discussion at $21.75-$22.50 for a five-day period late last week, the sources said.
September PJM power for firm, peak delivery was pegged at $21.70-22.40 with one unconfirmed trade at $21.90 per MWh, from talk at $21.50-$22.00 on Friday.
"The market was really undervalued for September," said one source.

October PJM prices, under the same delivery conditions, were discussed in a narrow range at $20.35-20.40 from $20.25-$20.50 on Friday, although there was little interest in October trade, the sources said.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
